step1_probe.source: Siril 1.4.4 src/stacking/median_and_mean.c compute_noise_weights(): pweights[layer][i] = 1/(coeff.pscale[layer][i]^2 * seq->stats[layer][idx]->bgnoise^2), normalized by the mean over frames per layer; bgnoise is the sequence's per-image statistic of the REGISTERED image; the only log line is 'Computing weights based on noise...' (no per-image weight is printed); docs preprocessing/stacking: 'Noise: weights individual frames based on background noise values.'
step1_probe.verdict: the zero-filled margins do NOT enter: the .seq statistics' ngoodpix equals the nonzero-pixel count of every registered image to the pixel, the .seq bgnoise equals Siril `bgnoise` on the whole registered frame, and the whole/centre-crop ratio is the member's own noise gradient (identical on the unregistered original: 1.119 vs 1.121 on july31); two side terms measured: resampling lowers a non-reference member's noise ~2.3 % (REG/ORIG 0.998/0.977/0.976), and the pscale term makes the weight (scale_i/(scale_ref*bgnoise_i))^2 — the member's dispersion-to-noise ratio squared — not 1/bgnoise^2 (probe implied weights G 0.889/1.031/1.080 vs 0.594/1.092/1.316 for 1/bgnoise^2)

predicted_weights.proxy: w ∝ (sqrt(BWMV)/bgnoise)^2 on the ORIGINAL member (Siril stat main + bgnoise, Green): sqrt(BWMV) stands in for the IKSS scale the addscale pscale uses (printed nowhere at full precision — 1 decimal here), so this is a DIRECTION, not the weight; the actual weights are reconstructed from the arm's r_s_.seq M lines after the build

actual_weights.formula: w_i = 1/(pscale_i^2 * bgnoise_i^2), pscale_i = scale_ref/scale_i, normalized by the mean over the 77 per layer (Siril 1.4.4 median_and_mean.c compute_noise_weights); every number from the kept r_s_.seq M lines (Siril's own registered-image statistics, nulls excluded: ngoodpix = the nonzero count)
